Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verses 1–2:

(p-663) Surat al-ʿAnkabut is Meccan, and it has sixty-nine verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Alif. Lam. Mim.﴾ ﴿Do people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and that they will not be tested?﴾ Al-ḥisbān (reckoning, supposition): it is the strength of one of two contradictories over the other, like ẓann (opinion), as opposed to shakk (doubt), which is standing between the two, and ʿilm (knowledge), which is certainty about one of them. These two (ḥisbān and ẓann) cannot be made to govern individual words (mufradāt), but only the contents of sentences (jumal). So if you say, "I reckoned Zayd, and I thought the horse," it means nothing until you say, "I reckoned Zayd knowledgeable, and I thought the horse swift," because your saying "Zayd is knowledgeable" and "the horse is swift" is a statement that signifies a content. So when you want to report that this content is established for you in the manner of opinion, not certainty, you introduce the verb of reckoning upon the two parts of the sentence, so that your purpose is complete. The sentence signifying the content that ḥisbān requires here is ﴿that they will be left [to say], "We believe," and that they will not be tested﴾. The meaning of its construction is: "Do they reckon that their being left, not tested, is for their saying, 'We believe'?" So "that they will be left" is the first object of ḥasiba, and "for their saying, 'We believe'" is the predicate; as for "not tested," it is the completion of "left," because it comes from tark (leaving) in the sense of taṣyīr (making), like the words of ʿAntarah:

"So I left him as food for the beasts, they gnawing him."

(p-664) Do you not see that before bringing in ḥisbān you could say, "Their being left, not tested, for their saying 'We believe'," with the supposition "established and settled" before the lām? And it is an interrogative of reproach. Fitnah (trial) means being tested by the hardships of obligation: leaving homelands, striving against enemies, all arduous acts of obedience, abstaining from desires, and by poverty, famine, and various calamities in lives and property, and enduring the disbelievers' harm and their plotting. It is narrated that it was revealed concerning some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who had become distressed by the harm of the polytheists, or concerning ʿAmmar ibn Yasir, who was being tortured for the sake of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 3:

﴿And We certainly tested﴾ means: We tried, tested. It is connected (mawsul) to aḥasiba (“did they think”) or to lā yuftanūna (“they will not be tested”). ﴿those who came before them﴾ with various kinds of trials. Among them was one whom a saw was placed upon his head, so that he was split into two halves; that did not turn him away from his religion. Among them was one who was combed with iron combs; that did not turn him away from his religion. ﴿So Allah will certainly know﴾ through the testing ﴿those who are truthful﴾ in faith, ﴿and He will certainly know the liars﴾ in it. The meaning of His knowledge, exalted is He, while He has always known that, is that He knows it as existing at the time of its existence, just as He knew before its existence that it would exist. The meaning is: the truthful among them will be distinguished from the liar. Ibn ʿAṭāʾ (Ibn ʿAṭāʾ) said: the truthfulness of the servant is made clear from his falsehood in times of ease and of affliction. Whoever gives thanks in days of ease and is patient in days of affliction is among the truthful; and whoever is arrogant in days of ease and anxious in days of affliction is among the liars.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 4:

﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that﴾

That is, polytheism (shirk) and sins (ma'asi). ﴿That they can outstrip Us﴾, i.e., that they can escape Us; meaning, that the recompense will surely overtake them. The fact that the relative clause (sila) of "an" (that) contains a predicate and a subject (musnad wa musnad ilayh) takes the place of the two objects (maf'ulayn), as in His saying: ﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. It is also permissible for "hasiba" (to think) to be construed with the meaning of "qaddara" (to suppose), and "am" (or) is then disjunctive (munqati'a), and the sense of the change of subject (al-idrab) in it is that this assumption is more baseless than the first assumption, because that one supposes that he will not be tested for his faith, whereas this one supposes that he will not be requited for his misdeeds. It is said that the first refers to the believers and this one to the disbelievers. ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾: "ma" (what) is in a position of nominative case (raf') in the sense of "evil is the judgment, their judgment," or in a position of accusative case (nasb) in the sense of "evil is a judgment they pass." The object of the dispraise is omitted, i.e., "wretched is the judgment they pass, their judgment."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 5:

﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾, i.e., hopes for His reward or fears His reckoning; hope admits of both. ﴿Then indeed the term of Allah﴾, the appointed time for reward and punishment, ﴿is surely coming﴾ without doubt. So let him hasten to righteous deeds that confirm his hope and fulfil his aspiration. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of what His servants say, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what they do, so nothing of it escapes Him.

Al-Zajjaj said: "man" (مَن) is a conditional particle, and it is in the nominative case by virtue of being the subject (mubtada'), and the answer of the condition is ﴿then indeed the term of Allah is surely coming﴾, like your saying: "If Zayd is in the house, then he has indeed fulfilled the promise."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 6:

﴿And whoever strives﴾ [against] his own self, through patient perseverance in obedience to Allah, or against Satan, by repelling his whisperings, or against the disbelievers, ﴿then he strives only for himself﴾, because the benefit of that returns to himself. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾, and free of need from their obedience and their striving. Rather, He commanded and forbade out of mercy for His servants.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 7:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will surely remove from them their misdeeds﴾, that is, polytheism (shirk) and sins, through faith and repentance (tawbah); ﴿and We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾, that is, the best reward for their deeds in Islam.

﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا﴾ *Wassā* (وصّى) has the same ruling as *amara* (أمر, "commanded") in meaning and in how it is used. It is said: *waṣṣaytu Zaydan bi-an yafʿala khayran* (وصّيْتُ زَيْدًا بِأنْ يَفْعَلَ خَيْرًا), just as you say: *amartuhu bi-an yafʿala* (أمَرْتُهُ بِأنْ يَفْعَلَ). From this is His saying: ﴿وَوَصّى بِها إبْراهِيمُ بَنِيهِ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 132], meaning: he instructed them with the word of *tawhid* (the Oneness of God) and commanded them to it. Your saying *waṣṣaytu Zaydan bi-ʿAmrin* (وصّيْتُ زَيْدًا بِعَمْرٍو) means: I instructed him to take care of ʿAmr and look after him, and the like. The same is the meaning of His saying ﴿وَوَصَّيْنا الإنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا﴾, and *wassaynāhu bi-ītāʾi wālidayhi ḥusnan* (ووَصَّيْناهُ بِإيتاءِ والِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا), or *bi-īlāʾi wālidayhi ḥusnan* (بِإيلاءِ والِدَيْهِ حُسْنًا), meaning: an act that is good, or [a thing] that is itself good because of its great goodness. This is like His saying ﴿وَقُولُوا لِلنّاسِ حُسْنًا﴾ [al-Baqarah: 83].

It is also permissible to make *ḥusnan* (حُسْنًا) fall under the same construction as your saying *Zaydan* (زَيْدًا) with an implied verb, as when you see someone preparing to strike and say *Zaydan iḍrib* (زَيْدًا اضْرِبْ). Here one supplies the verb: *awlihimā* (أوْلِهِما, "do good to them"), *aʿṭihimā* (أعْطِهِما, "give to them"), or *if ʿal bihimā ḥusnan* (افْعَلْ بِهِما حُسْنًا, "act toward them with goodness"), because the commandment regarding them indicates it, and what follows agrees with it. It is as if he said: "We said: do good to them, and do not obey them in polytheism if they urge you toward it."

On this explanation, if one pauses (*waqf*, a pause in recitation) at ﴿بِوالِدَيْهِ﴾ and begins (*ibtidāʾ*, starting a new phrase) with ﴿حُسْنًا﴾, the pause is good. On the first explanation, it is necessary to supply the verb "say" (*al-qawl*), meaning: "And We said:"

﴿وَإنْ جاهَداكَ﴾ O human, ﴿لِتُشْرِكَ بِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾, meaning: there is no knowledge of His divinity. The intended meaning of the negation of knowledge is the negation of the known object. It is as if He said: "to make partners with Me something that cannot be a god." ﴿فَلا تُطِعْهُما﴾ in that matter, for there is no obedience to a created being in disobedience to the Creator. ﴿إلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ﴾, the return of all of you, both those who believed among you and those who associated partners [with God]. ﴿فَأُنَبِّئُكم بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾, so I will recompense you in full measure of your recompense. In the mention of the return and the threat there is a warning against following the two in polytheism, and an exhortation to steadfastness and uprightness in the religion.

It is narrated that when Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas (سَعْدَ بْنَ أبِي وقّاصٍ) embraced Islam, his mother vowed that she would neither eat nor drink until he apostatized. So he complained to the Prophet (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed. The [verses] in Luqman and in al-Ahqaf are the other [similar] ones.

﴿Those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is the *mubtada'* (the subject of the nominal sentence), and the *khabar* (the predicate) is ﴿We will certainly admit them among the righteous﴾, meaning among their company. Righteousness (*salah*) is one of the most eloquent attributes of the believers, and it is what the prophets (peace be upon them) most desired. Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: ﴿And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants﴾ [al-Naml: 19]. And Yusuf (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Cause me to die in submission, and join me with the righteous﴾ [Yusuf: 101]. Or it means the place of entry of the righteous, which is Paradise.

It was revealed concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And among people is one who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the sake of Allah﴾, i.e., when harm from the disbelievers touches him, ﴿he regards the trial of people as the punishment of Allah﴾, i.e., (p-667) he panics at it just as one panics at the punishment of Allah the Exalted. ﴿But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you"﴾, i.e., when Allah grants victory to the believers and they gain spoils, they confront them and say, "Indeed, we were with you," meaning: we were following you in your religion, steadfast upon it through your steadfastness, so give us our share of the spoils. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds?﴾, i.e., He is most knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds, from among the worlds, with respect to what is in their breasts. Among that is what is in the breasts of these people of hypocrisy, and what is in the breasts of the believers of sincerity. Then He promised the believers and threatened the hypocrites with His saying.
And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites. That is: their condition is manifest to the One who holds the requital for both of them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 12:

﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins."﴾ They commanded them to follow their way, which is their path that they were upon in their religion, and they commanded themselves to bear their sins. So he conjoined the command to the command (fa-ʿataffa al-amr ʿalā al-amr), and they intended that these two matters be combined in attainment: that you follow our way and that we bear your sins. The meaning is that the bearing of the burden is conditional upon following, i.e., if you follow our way, we will bear your sins. This is the statement of the chieftains of Quraysh, who would say to whoever among them believed: "We will not be resurrected, nor will you. If that is so, then we will bear your sin on your behalf." ﴿But they are not at all bearers of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.﴾ This is because they said that while their hearts were contrary to it, like the liars who promise a thing while in their hearts there is the intention of breaking it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 13:

﴿And they will surely bear their burdens﴾, i.e., the burdens of their own selves, meaning their sins because of their disbelief. ﴿And other burdens along with their burdens﴾, i.e., other burdens besides the sins for which they guaranteed the believers to bear, and these are the burdens of those who were a cause of their going astray. And this is as He said: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ [al-Nahl: 25] (p-668). ﴿And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to fabricate﴾, i.e., what they invented of lies and falsehoods.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 14:

﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years.﴾ His lifespan was one thousand and fifty years. He was sent (as a prophet) at the age of forty, and he remained among his people nine hundred and fifty years, and he lived sixty years after the Flood. And it is related from Wahb that he lived one thousand four hundred years, and the Angel of Death said to him: "O longest-lived of the prophets, how did you find the world?" He said: "Like a house that has two doors: I entered and I exited."

He did not say "nine hundred and fifty years," because if it had been said that way, it could have been imagined that this number applies to most of it. This imagining is removed here, so it is as though it were said "nine hundred and fifty years, complete and exact in number," except that this is more concise, sweeter in expression, and fuller in benefit. Also, the story was brought to console our Prophet (ﷺ) for what Noah (peace be upon him) was tested with from his community and for what he endured of the long patience, as consolation for our Prophet (ﷺ). Thus mentioning "a thousand" is more majestic and more effective in reaching the purpose. The specifying noun was introduced first with "years" and then with "general" (ʿām), because repeating one word within one utterance is something to be avoided in eloquence.

﴿So the Flood seized them﴾: it is what surrounds and encompasses with abundance and overpowering force, such as a torrent of water, or the darkness of night, or the like of these two.

﴿while they were wrongdoers﴾: toward their own selves, by disbelief.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 15:**

﴿So We rescued him﴾, that is, Nuh (Noah), ﴿and the companions of the Ark﴾. They were seventy-eight persons, half of them male and half of them female, among them the sons of Nuh: Sam, Ham and Yafith, and their wives. ﴿And We made it﴾, that is, the Ark, or the event, or the story, ﴿a sign﴾, a lesson and an admonition, ﴿for the worlds﴾, who take warning from it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 16:

﴿And Ibrahim﴾ is in the accusative by the implied verb "mention" (udhkur), and "when he said" (idh qala) substitutes for it as a badal ishtimal (inclusive substitute), because times include what occurs in them. Or it is conjoined to Nuh, meaning: "And We sent Ibrahim." Or it is an adverbial complement (zarf) of "We sent," meaning: "We sent him when he reached an age or a level of knowledge suitable for him to admonish his people and command them to worship and piety (p-669)." Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Abu Hanifa – may Allah be pleased with them both – read "wa-Ibrahimu" with a nominative vowel, meaning: "And among the messengers is Ibrahim." ﴿He said to his people: Worship Allah and fear Him. That is better for you﴾ than disbelief, ﴿if you knew﴾, that is, if you had knowledge of what is better for you than what is worse for you.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, you worship besides Allah idols (awthan)﴾ — idols (asnam) — ﴿and you fabricate﴾ — and you lie, or you make (taslna'un). Abu Hudhayfa and al-Sulami — may Allah be pleased with them both — recited "wa-tukhalliqun," from khalqa with the sense of intensification (al-takthir) in khalaqa, ﴿a falsehood (ifkan)﴾. It is also read "afikan," which is a verbal noun (masdar) like kadhib and la'ib. Al-ifk is a lightened form of it, like al-kidhb and al-li'b from their roots. Their fabrication of falsehood (ikhtilaquhum al-ifk) is their naming the idols gods (alihah) and partners (shuraka') of Allah.

﴿Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you provision (rizq)﴾ — they are unable to provide you with any of the provision — ﴿so seek provision from Allah﴾ — all of it — for He is the Provider alone; none other provides. ﴿And worship Him and give thanks to Him; to Him you will be returned﴾ — so prepare yourselves for meeting Him by worshipping Him and thanking Him for His blessings. And with a fatha on the ta' and a kasra on the jim, it is read by Ya'qub (tarji'un).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 18:

﴿And if you deny, then nations before you have denied, and the Messenger's duty is only clear conveyance.﴾ I.e.: And if you deny me, your denial will not harm me, for the messengers before me were denied by their peoples, and they did not harm them. Rather, they harmed only themselves, when the punishment descended upon them because of their denial. As for the Messenger, his affair is complete, since he conveyed the clear message (al-balagh al-mubin), with which doubt departs, and that is its being accompanied by the signs (ayat) of God and His miracles (mu'jizat). Or: And if I am denied among you, then I have in the rest of the prophets an example (uswa), since they were denied. The Messenger's duty is to convey, and his duty is not to be believed or to be not denied. This verse and the verses that follow it, up to His saying ﴿So what was the answer of his people﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24] (p-670), may be part of the speech of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, to his people, and the meaning of "the nations before him" is the people of Shith, Idris, Nuh and others. Or they may be verses that came as an interjection (mu'tarida) concerning the affair of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the affair of Quraysh, placed between the beginning and the end of the story of Ibrahim. If you say: interjected sentences (al-jumal al-i'tiradiyya, sentences inserted parenthetically) must have a connection to that in which they are interjected, so you do not say: "Makkah — and Zayd is standing — is the best of God's lands." I say: yes, and its explanation is that the mention of the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, is nothing but intended to ease the distress of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and to be a consolation to him, in that his forefather Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was tested in a manner similar to what he was tested with, namely the polytheism of his people and their worship of idols. So he interjected with His saying ﴿And if you deny﴾, with the meaning: "O assembly of Quraysh, if you deny Muhammad, then Ibrahim denied his people, and every nation denied its prophet," because His saying ﴿nations before you have denied﴾ must include the nation of Ibrahim. And this, as you see, is a connected interjection. Then all the verses after it are its continuations, because they speak of tawhid and its proofs, the demolition of polytheism, the weakening of its foundations, the attribute of God's power and dominion, and the clarity of His proof and evidence.

﴿Have they not seen﴾. Reading it with the taʼ (تَرَوْا, "have you not seen") is the reading of al-Kufiyyun other than Hafs. ﴿how Allah originates creation﴾, that is, they have indeed seen that and known it. His saying ﴿then He repeats it﴾ is not conjoined to "originates" (yubdi'u), and the seeing does not fall upon it; rather it is an independent statement about the repetition after death, just as the looking occurs in His saying ﴿See how He originated creation; then Allah will produce the final creation﴾ [al-ʻAnkabut: 20], where the looking falls upon the origination and not upon the producing. Rather, it is conjoined to the whole clause of His saying ﴿Have they not seen how Allah originates creation﴾. ﴿Indeed that﴾, i.e., the repetition, ﴿is easy for Allah﴾, that is, simple.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 20:

﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad. Even if it is from the words of Ibrahim, its implied meaning is: "We revealed to him that he should say," ﴿Travel through the earth and observe how He originated creation﴾, despite their multitude and the diversity of their conditions, so that you may come to know through direct observation the wonders of God's originating activity (fitra). "Bada'a" and "abda'a" have the same meaning. ﴿Then God brings forth the final creation﴾, that is, the resurrection. It is read with a long vowel (madd) where it occurs in the reading of Makki (Ibn Jurayj) and Abu 'Amr. This (p-671) is evidence that they are two creations, and that each of them is an initiation (inshā'), that is, a beginning, an innovation, and a bringing forth from non-existence into existence. However, the final creation is an initiation after an initiation similar to it, whereas the first is not like that. The analogical form would be to say: "How did God originate creation, then God brings forth the final creation." But it was said, "How He originated creation, then God brings forth the final creation," because the discourse with them concerned repetition (ihada). When He established for them that the first origination was from God, He argued against them that repetition is an initiation like origination. So if origination does not defeat Him, repetition must not defeat Him either. It is as if He said: "Then that One who brought forth the first creation is the One who brings forth the final creation." To draw attention to this meaning, He made His name prominent and placed it as the subject (mubtada'). ﴿Indeed God is over all things Powerful﴾, capable.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 21:

﴿He punishes whom He wills﴾ by abandonment (al-khidhlan), ﴿and has mercy on whom He wwills﴾ by guidance, or by greed and contentment, or by bad character and good character, or by turning away from God and turning toward Him, or by following innovations (bida') and by adhering to the Sunnah. ﴿And to Him you will be turned back﴾, meaning you will be returned and brought back.

"And you cannot escape (Allah) ﴿in the earth﴾ (the wide expanse) ﴿nor in the heaven﴾, which is wider and more spacious than it, even if you were in it. ﴿And you have not, besides Allah, any protector﴾ who would manage your affairs ﴿nor any helper﴾, nor any supporter who would prevent you from My punishment."

﴿Those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah﴾ (by His proofs of His oneness, His books, and His miracles), ﴿and in His meeting, those have despaired of My mercy﴾ (My Paradise), ﴿and for them there is a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 24:

﴿So there was no answer from his people﴾ — the people of Ibrahim (Abraham), when he invited them to faith — ﴿except that they said: "Kill him or burn him."﴾ Some of them said to others, or one of them said it while the rest were content, so they were all, in ruling, among those who said it, and they agreed upon burning him. ﴿But Allah saved him from the fire﴾ (p-672) when they threw him into it. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ — in what they did to him and what We did. It is related that on that day the fire was not made use of, meaning the day Ibrahim was cast into the fire, and that was because its heat had gone.

Ibrahim said to his people, ﴿You have only taken idols besides Allah as a bond of affection between you in the life of this world﴾. Hamza and Hafs [read it as] "مَوَدَّةَ بَيْنِكُمْ". "مَوَدَّةً بَيْنَكُمْ": Madani, Shami, Hammad, Yahya and Khalaf. "مَوَدَّةُ بَيْنِكُمْ": Makki, Basri and Ali. "مَوَدَّةٌ بَيْنَكُمُ": al-Shamuni and al-Barjami.

The accusative (al-nasb) has two possibilities. The first is that it is a causal (ta'lil) construction, meaning: so that you may show affection to one another and keep ties with one another, because you have gathered in worshipping them and agreed upon them, just as people agree on a school of thought, and this becomes the cause of their mutual love. The second is that it is a second object (maf'ul thani), as in His saying, ﴿Has taken his own desire as his god﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23]. The particle "ma" is *kaffah* (the particle that stops its governing force), meaning: you have taken the idols as the cause of affection between you, with an elided modifier (al-mudaf), or you have taken them as an affection between you, meaning as something loved between you, as in His saying, ﴿And among people are those who take, besides Allah, rivals whom they love as they love Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165].

As for the nominative (al-raf'), there are two possibilities. It may be the predicate of "inna", with "ma" being a relative pronoun (mawsulah). Or it may be the predicate of an elided subject (mubtada'), meaning: "it is affection between you." The meaning is that the idols are affection between you, meaning something loved, or a cause of affection.

Whoever makes "al-mawaddah" a genitive construction (idafah) treats "baynakum" as a noun and not as an adverb of place, as in His saying, ﴿The testimony between you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 106]. Whoever applies tanwin to "mawaddatan" and puts "baynakum" in the accusative, then it is an adverb of place (zarf).

﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disavow others﴾: the idols will disown their worshippers. ﴿And some of you will curse others﴾: meaning, on the Day of Resurrection mutual cursing will take place among you, so the followers will curse the leaders. ﴿And your refuge is the Fire﴾: meaning, the abode of the worshipper and the worshipped, and of the follower and the followed. ﴿And you will have no helpers﴾: there.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 26:

﴿So Lut believed in him﴾ — that is, in Ibrahim (peace be upon him). ﴿Lut﴾ — he is the son of the brother of Ibrahim, and he was the first to believe in him when he saw that the fire did not burn him. ﴿And he [Ibrahim] said﴾ (p-673) ﴿"Indeed I am a emigrant﴾ from Kawtha, which is in the outskirts of Kufa, to Harran, and then from there to Filastin (Palestine), which is part of the desert of al-Sham (Greater Syria). For this reason they said: every prophet has a hijrah (emigration), but Ibrahim has two emigrations. With him in his emigration were Lut and Sarah, and Ibrahim had married her. ﴿To my Lord﴾ — to wherever my Lord has commanded me to emigrate to Him. ﴿Indeed He is the Almighty﴾ — the One who protects me from my enemies. ﴿the All-Wise﴾ — the One who commands me only to do what is good."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 27:

﴿And We bestowed upon him Isaac﴾ as a son, ﴿and Jacob﴾ as a grandson; and he did not mention Isma'il because of his fame. ﴿And We placed in his descendants prophethood﴾, that is, among the descendants of Abraham, for he is the tree of the prophets. ﴿And the Book﴾, and what is meant by it is the category (jins), that is: the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms and the Furqan. ﴿And We gave him his reward﴾, that is, Abraham: good commendation, blessings upon him until the end of time, and the love of the adherents of the religions for him. Or it is the continuation of his hospitality at his grave, and this is not for anyone else. ﴿in this world﴾: in it is evidence that God, exalted is He, may give the reward in this world. ﴿And indeed he is in the Hereafter among the righteous﴾, that is, among the people of Paradise. From al-Hasan:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 28:

﴿And Lot⦆ — i.e., remember Lot, ﴿when he said to his people: "Indeed you commit an abomination (al-fahisha), an act extreme in its ugliness, and it is sodomy (al-lutwa)"﴾ ﴿"No one among the worlds has preceded you in it."﴾ This is a resumed sentence (jumla mustan'afa) that establishes the abomination of that act, as if a questioner had asked: why was it an abomination? So it was said: because no one before them had undertaken it. They said: no male had ever mounted a male before the people of Lot.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 29:

﴿Do you indeed approach men, and cut off the way﴾ by killing and seizing property, as the highwaymen do. It is also said that their "cutting off the way" was their waylaying of passers-by with indecency. ﴿And you commit the evil﴾ in your gathering-place (nadi, i.e. your assembly). The word nadi is not applied to a gathering unless its people are still present in it. ﴿The evil﴾ means: sodomy (al-mudarrata), intercourse (al-mujama'a), reviling (al-subab), obscenity in jest (al-fuhsh fi al-mizah), pelting one another with pebbles (al-hadhf bi al-hasa), (p-674) chewing gum (mad'gh al-'alk), snapping the fingers (al-farqa'a), and using the miswak among people. ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said: "Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful"﴾ regarding what you threaten us with of the descent of the punishment.

"A-innakum" (with the second hamza as a hamza, i.e. "a-innakum") is read by Ibn 'Amir and Hafs, and this is the reading found in the Imam (the 'Uthmani codex). Each of them with two hamzas is the reading of the Kufans except Hafs. "A-ynnakum" with a long (madd) hamza followed by a short kasra-vowelled ya is the reading of Abu 'Amr. "Ayinnakum" with a short (qasr) hamza followed by a kasra-vowelled ya is the reading of Makki, Nafi' (except Qalun), Sahl, and Ya'qub (except Zayd).

"He said: My Lord, help me against the people who spread corruption"—by sending down punishment upon them, "against the corrupt people." They used to corrupt people by driving them to the sins and abominations they themselves were engaged in.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 31:

﴿And when Our messengers came to Ibrahim with the good news,﴾ with the glad tidings to Ibrahim of a son, and [of] the grandson (al-nafilah), namely Ishaq and Ya'qub. ﴿They said, "Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town."﴾ The construction "muhlikū" (destroyers) with the genitive "ahl" does not yield definiteness, because it carries the meaning of the future. "The town" is Sodom, of which it was said, "More unjust than the judge of Sodom." This town indicates that it was near the place of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. It is said that it was a day and a night's journey from the place of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. ﴿Indeed, its people were wrongdoers.﴾ That is, the wrongdoing had persisted among them in the past days, and they were persistent in it, and their wrongdoing was their disbelief and various kinds of their sins.

[Qur'anic text:] ﴿He said, "Indeed, within it is Lot."﴾ That is: Will you destroy them while among them is one who is innocent of wrongdoing, namely Lot? ﴿They said﴾ — that is, the angels — ﴿"We are most knowing﴾ than you ﴿of who is within it. We will surely save him﴾ — "linunjiyannahu" (we will surely save him) is read by Ya'qub and the Kufans other than ʿĀṣim (p. 675) ﴿and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remain﴾ — those left behind in the punishment.

Then He informed about the journey of the angels to Lot after their parting from Ibrahim, with His saying:

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 29, verse 33:**

﴿And when Our messengers came to Lut, he was distressed on their account.﴾ *Sāʾahu majīʾuhum* (it grieved him that they came). *Wa-anna* is a connective particle (*ṣila*) that emphasizes the occurrence of the two actions, one following the other, as if they occurred within a single moment of time. It is as if it were said: as soon as he perceived their coming, distress overtook him without delay, out of fear for them from his people, that they would assault them with immorality. The reading *"sīʾa bihim"* is attributed to the Madinan, the Syrian and ʿAlī (the reading transmitted through them is a *qirāʾa*, a canonical recitation variant).

﴿And he was constrained by them in his resources.﴾ He was straitened by their affair and by the management of their matter; *dharʿuhu* means his capacity (*ṭāqatuhu*). They used the narrowness of the *dharʿ* (the forearm, here meaning capacity) and the *dhirāʿ* as an expression for the loss of capacity, just as they say *raḥb al-dharʿ* (broad of forearm) when a person is capable. The original basis of this is that when a man's arm is long, he attains what a short-armed man cannot attain; so this was made a figure of speech for incapacity and capability. The word is in the accusative as a specification (*tamyīz*, a grammatical term meaning a noun that clarifies the ambiguity of a preceding word).

﴿And they said: "Do not fear, nor grieve; indeed we will deliver you and your family,﴾ and with the lightening of the consonant (*tanjiyuka* with the lightened form, reading *munajjūka*) it is read by the Meccan and the Kufan readers other than Ḥafṣ. *Wa-ahlaka* (and your family): the *kāf* is in the genitive position, and *ahlaka* is in the accusative by an omitted verb, meaning: and We will deliver your family.﴾ ﴿Except your wife; she was among those who remained behind.﴾

﴿Indeed, We are sending down﴾ (*munazzilun*, the reading of al-Shami, i.e. Ibn 'Amir, one of the canonical reciters) ﴿upon the people of this town a punishment﴾ (*rijzan*, meaning a torment) ﴿from the sky, because of what they were doing of defiance (*yafsuqun*)﴾, that is, because of their defiance and their departure from obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

And We have certainly left of it (of the town) a clear sign (هي آثارُ مَنازِلِهِمُ الخَرِبَةِ: it is the remains of their ruined dwellings; وقِيلَ: and it was said: الماءُ الأسْوَدُ عَلى وجْهِ الأرْضِ: it is the black water upon the surface of the earth) for a people who understand (يَتَعَلَّقُ بِتَرَكْنا أوْ بِ"بَيِّنَةً": this relates either to "We left" or to "clear").

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 36:

﴿And to Madyan﴾ We sent to Madyan ﴿their brother Shu'ayb. He said: "O my people, worship Allah and hope for the Last Day,"﴾ and act in a way by which you hope for reward in the outcome, or fear it. ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption﴾ intending corruption.

﴿So they denied him, and the quake seized them.﴾ It was the severe earthquake, or the Cry of Jibril (peace be upon him), because the hearts quaked from it. ﴿So they became in their abode﴾ in their town and their land ﴿prostrate, crouching on their knees﴾ dead.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 38:

﴿And ʿAd⁠﴾ is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb, "We destroyed" (ahlaknā), because His saying ﴿So the earthquake seized them⁠﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 37] indicates it, since it carries the meaning of destruction. ﴿And Thamud⁠﴾: Hamzah, Hafs, Sahl and Yaʿqub read it in the genitive... ﴿And it has become clear to you⁠﴾ that is, what He has described of their destruction ﴿from their dwellings⁠﴾, meaning from the direction of their dwellings, which you see when you pass by them, and the people of Makkah used to pass by them on their journeys and would see them. ﴿And Satan made their deeds appear fair to them⁠﴾, namely the disbelief and sins. ﴿And he barred them from the way⁠﴾, the way they were commanded to follow, which is faith in Allah and His messengers. ﴿And they were discerning⁠﴾, meaning intelligent, able to reflect and to distinguish truth from falsehood, but they did not do so.

Qur'an 29:39 (Commentary of al-Nasafi, Madarik al-Tanzil):

﴿And Qarun, and Pharaoh, and Haman⦆ i.e., and We destroyed them. ﴿And Musa had certainly come to them with clear proofs, but they acted arrogantly in the land, and they were not ones who could escape⦆ i.e., those who could outpace (sabiqin, "escaping"); the command of Allah overtook them, so they could not get away from it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 40:

﴿So each We seized for his sin.﴾ In it is a refutation of those who permit punishment without sin. ﴿Among them are those upon whom We sent a violent wind with pebbles.﴾ It is a strong wind in which there are pebbles, and it was for the people of Lot. ﴿And among them are those who were seized by the Blast.﴾ It was for Madyan and Thamud. ﴿And among them are those whom We caused the earth to swallow.﴾ He means Qarun. ﴿And among them are those whom We drowned.﴾ He means the people of Noah and Pharaoh. ﴿And Allah would not have wronged them,﴾ by punishing them without sin. ﴿But they were wronging themselves,﴾ through disbelief and transgression.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 41:**

﴿The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah﴾, i.e., gods. That is, it is the likeness of one who associates others with Allah, the idols, in weakness and poor choice. ﴿is like the spider, which takes a house﴾, i.e., it is like the spider in what it takes for itself as a house. Indeed, that is a house that does not keep off heat or cold, and does not protect from what houses protect from. Likewise, the idols do not benefit them in this world or the Hereafter. Hatim made "took" (ittakhadhat) a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative, a grammatical term for a word describing the state of the subject at the time of the action). ﴿And indeed, the frailest of houses is the spider's house﴾, meaning there is no house frailer than its house. It is reported from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "Clean your houses of spider webs, for leaving them brings poverty." ﴿If only they knew﴾ that this is their likeness, and that the matter of their religion reaches this extreme of frailty.

It has also been said that the meaning of the verse is: the likeness of the polytheist who worships an idol, compared with the believer who worships Allah, is like a spider that takes a house, compared with a man who builds a house of baked brick and plaster, or carves it from rock. Just as the frailest of houses, when you examine them house by house, is the spider's house, so too the weakest of religions, when you examine them religion by religion, is the worship of idols. ﴿If only they knew.﴾

al-Zajjaj and a group of scholars said: the sense of the verse is: ﴿The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah﴾ ﴿if only they knew﴾ ﴿is like the spider.﴾

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 42:

﴿Indeed, Allah knows what they call upon﴾ — with the ya' (i.e., yaʿlamu with the third-person prefix), read by Basri, and ʿAsim except al-A'sha and al-Barjami. Here "ma" (what) is in the sense of "alladhi" (that which), and it is the object of "yaʿlamu" (knows). The object of "yadʿūna" (they call upon) is a pronoun attached to it, meaning: "yaʿbudūnahu" (they worship it).

﴿besides Allah, of anything﴾ — the "min" in "min shay'" (of anything) is for specification (li-l-tabyin).

﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ — the Overpowering, who has no partner. ﴿the All-Wise﴾ — in withholding hasty punishment. In this there is a rebuke for them, since they worshipped an inanimate object that has no knowledge and no power, and abandoned the worship of the One who is capable and dominant over everything, the All-Wise who does nothing except with wisdom and governance.

The word الأمثال (al-amthal, "the parables") is a نَعْتٌ (na't, a descriptive qualifier), and the predicate (الخَبَرُ, al-khabar) is نَضْرِبُها (nadribuha, "We strike them"), meaning نُبَيِّنُها (nubayyinuha, "We make them clear"). ﴿And these parables﴾ ﴿We set forth for the people﴾ ﴿but none understands them except those who have knowledge﴾ ... The foolish and ignorant ones among the Quraysh used to say, "Indeed the Lord of Muhammad strikes parables with the fly and the spider," and they would laugh at this. Therefore Allah said: ﴿and none understands them except those who have knowledge﴾ of Him, His names and His attributes. That is, none comprehends their soundness and excellence or grasps their benefit except those people, because parables and comparisons are only the paths to hidden meanings, to bring them out and present them to the understanding. Just as this comparison depicts the difference between the state of the polytheist and the state of the monotheist. It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited this verse and said: "The scholar is the one who understands from Allah and acts in obedience to Him and avoids His displeasure." The verse also indicates the superiority of knowledge ('ilm) over intellect ('aql).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 44:

﴿Allah created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾ That is: muhiqqan (in truth), meaning: He did not create them in vain, but for a wisdom, which is that they should be dwellings for His servants, and a lesson for those among them who take heed, and signs of the greatness of His power. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers﴾? He singled them out for mention because they are the ones who benefit from them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 45:

﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾, seeking nearness to Allah, Exalted, by reciting His speech, and so that you may stand upon what He has commanded and forbidden. ﴿And establish the prayer﴾, i.e., persist in establishing the prayer. ﴿Indeed, the prayer forbids immorality﴾, the ugly deed, such as fornication for example, ﴿and wrongdoing﴾. The munkar (wrongdoing) is that which the Sharia and reason deem objectionable. It has been said: whoever observes the prayer, that will lead him, in time, to refrain from evil deeds. It has been narrated: "It was said one day to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'So-and-so prays by day and steals by night.' He said: 'His prayer will surely restrain him.'" And it has been narrated: "A young man from the Ansar used to pray the prayers with him, yet he did not leave any of the obscenities without committing it. It was described to him (the Prophet), and he said: 'His prayer will soon restrain him.' He did not linger before he repented." Ibn 'Awf said: "Prayer forbids when you are in it; you are in what is good and obedience, and it has held you back from immorality and wrongdoing." From al-Hasan: "Whoever his prayer does not restrain from immorality and wrongdoing, his prayer is not a prayer, and it is a burden upon him." ﴿And the remembrance of Allah is greater﴾, i.e., the prayer is greater than other acts of obedience. He said "and the remembrance of Allah" only so that it stands independently as the reason, as if he had said: "And the prayer is greater, because it is the remembrance of Allah." From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "And the remembrance of Allah of you by His mercy is greater than your remembrance of Him by your obedience." Ibn 'Ata said: "The remembrance of Allah of you is greater than your remembrance of Him, because His remembrance is without cause, whereas your remembrance is mixed with causes and wishful thinking, and because His remembrance does not perish, whereas your remembrance does not last." Salman said: "The remembrance of Allah is greater and more excellent than everything." For the Prophet ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of your deeds, the purest of them in the sight of your King, the highest of them in your ranks, and better for you than giving gold and silver, and better than meeting your enemy, striking their necks and them striking yours?" They said: "What is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The remembrance of Allah." And he was asked which deed is best, and he said: "That you depart this world with your tongue moist with the remembrance of Allah." Or: the remembrance of Allah is greater than what your understandings and minds can contain. Or: the remembrance of Allah is greater than that any disobedience should remain alongside it. Or: the remembrance of Allah is greater in forbidding immorality and wrongdoing than anything else. ﴿And Allah knows what you do﴾, of good and obedience, so He will reward you with the best of rewards.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 46:

﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾ with the manner that is best, which is to meet harshness with gentleness and anger with restraint, as He said: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better﴾ [Fussilat: 34]. (﴿Except those of them who have wronged﴾) who have gone to excess in aggression and obstinacy, who did not accept counsel, and for whom gentleness was of no benefit, so harshness was applied to them. It was also said: ﴿except those who harmed the Messenger of Allah﴾ (ﷺ), or ﴿except those who attributed a son and a partner [to Allah] and said, "The hand of Allah is chained"﴾. Or its meaning is: Do not argue with those who have entered the protection covenant (dhimma) and pay the poll tax (jizya) except in the best manner; except those who have wronged, who renounced the covenant and withheld the jizya, for arguing with them is by the sword. The verse indicates the permissibility of debate (munazara) with disbelievers regarding religion, and the permissibility of learning the science of theology (ilm al-kalam), by which argumentation is achieved. His saying ﴿And say, "We believe in what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you. Our God and your God is one, and to Him we are Muslims"﴾ is of the same kind as arguing in the best manner. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Do not believe the People of the Book when they relate to you, nor deny them, but say: "We believe in Allah and His books and His messengers." If it is false, you have not confirmed it, and if it is true, you have not denied it.»

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 47:

﴿And thus﴾ like that sending down, ﴿We have sent down to you the Book﴾; that is, We sent it down confirming the rest of the heavenly Books, or: just as We sent down Books to those before you, so We sent down the Book to you. ﴿Those to whom We have given the Book believe in it﴾: they are ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and those with him. ﴿And among these﴾, that is, among the people of Makkah, ﴿there are some who believe in it.﴾ Or the intended meaning of "those given the Book" is those among the People of the Book who preceded the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and "these" are those who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. ﴿And none deny Our signs﴾ despite their being manifest and the doubt about them having been removed, ﴿except the disbelievers﴾: except those who plunge deeply into disbelief and are determined upon it, such as Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and his like. (p. 681)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 48:

﴿And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾. "Before it" means before the Qur'an. The right hand is singled out because writing is generally done with the right hand. The meaning is: you had not read any of the books, and you were not a writer.

﴿Otherwise﴾, that is, had any of that been the case, namely reciting or writing, ﴿the falsifiers would have doubted﴾. These are the falsifiers among the People of the Book, who would have said: "The one whose description we find in our books is an unlettered man who neither writes nor reads, and he is not him." Or it refers to the polytheists of Mecca, who would have said: "Perhaps he learned it or wrote it with his own hand." He called them "falsifiers" because of their denial of his prophethood.

It is related from Mujahid and al-Sha'bi that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not die until he had learned to write and to read.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 49:**

﴿Rather, it﴾ — i.e., the Qur'an — ﴿is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾ — i.e., in the breasts of the scholars of it (ʿulamāʾ bihi) and its memorizers (ḥuffāẓuhu). These two are among the distinctive features of the Qur'an: that its verses are clear in their inimitability (iʿjāz), and that it is preserved in the breasts (ṣudūr), unlike other books, for they were not miracles, nor were they recited except from codices (maṣāḥif). ﴿And none deny Our signs﴾ — the manifest ones — ﴿except the wrongdoers﴾ — i.e., those who plunge deeply into wrongdoing (al-mutawaghghilūna fī al-ẓulm).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 50:

﴿وَقالُوا لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ آياتٌ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾ "Āyatun" (آيَةٌ) without an alif is the reading of Ibn Kathir (Makki) and of the Kufans other than Hafs; they intended: "Why are not signs (āyāt) sent down upon him?" The signs meant are like the she-camel (of Salih), the staff (of Musa), the table spread (of ʿIsa), and the like, ʿalayhimu l-salam. ﴿Say: Indeed, the signs are with God﴾; He sends down whichever He wills, and I possess none of them. ﴿And I am only a clear warner﴾; I have been charged with warning and with making it clear by means of the signs I have been given, and it is not for me to say, "Send down upon me a sign of such-and-such, rather than a sign of such-and-such," since I know that what is meant by the signs is the establishment of proof, and all the signs are equal in that respect.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 51:

﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, which is recited to them?﴾ That is: is it not sufficient for them a sign that suffices in place of all other signs, if they are seekers of the truth and not obstinate challengers, namely this Qur'an, whose recitation endures among them in every place and time, so that there remains with them a constant sign (p-682) that does not vanish as every sign vanishes after its occurrence, or that exists in one place but not another? ﴿Indeed, in that﴾ — that is, in this sign which exists in every place and time until the end of the age — ﴿is surely a mercy﴾, a great blessing, ﴿and a reminder﴾, an admonition, ﴿for a people who believe﴾, as opposed to the obstinate challengers.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 52:

﴿Say: "Allah suffices as a witness between me and you."﴾ That is: a witness to the truth of what I claim concerning the message and the sending down of the Qur'an upon me, and to your denial. ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ So He is aware of my affair and your affair, and knows my truth and your falsehood. ﴿And those who believe in falsehood﴾ among you, which is what they worship besides Allah, ﴿and disbelieve in Allah﴾ and His signs, ﴿it is they who are the losers.﴾ They are the ones who are cheated in their bargain, since they have exchanged disbelief for faith. However, the statement came in the manner of fairness, like His saying: ﴿And indeed, either we or you are upon guidance or in clear error﴾ [Saba': 24]. It is narrated that Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions said: "O Muhammad, who will testify for you that you are the Messenger of Allah?" So this verse was revealed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 53:

﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾ by their saying ﴿"Rain down upon us stones from the sky"﴾ [al-Anfal: 32], and so on. ﴿Had there not been a specified term﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of Badr, or the time of their perishing at their appointed times. The meaning is: Had there not been a term that Allah has named and specified in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh), He would have punished them, and wisdom requires delaying it until that specified term. ﴿The punishment would have come upon them﴾ immediately. ﴿And it will surely come upon them﴾ immediately, or ﴿will it surely come upon them﴾ at the specified term? ﴿Suddenly﴾, unexpectedly, ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ the time of its coming.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 54:

﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell will surround the disbelievers.﴾ That is: it will surround them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 55:

﴿On the Day the punishment will envelop them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾, like His saying, ﴿Above them will be layers of fire, and beneath them layers﴾ [al-Zumar: 16]. There is no pause at ﴿disbelievers﴾ [al-Ankabut: 54], because "the Day" (yawm) is an adverbial complement (zarf) of the encompassing of the Fire around them. ﴿And He will say﴾ with the yāʾ (i.e., yaqūlu, in the third person) is the reading of al-Kufiyyun and Nafi‘. His saying ﴿Taste what you used to do﴾ means: the recompense for your deeds.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 56:**

﴿O My servants who believe﴾. The reading with the ya' unvocalized (sukun) is that of Basran and Kufan readers other than ʿĀṣim. ﴿Indeed My earth is vast﴾. The reading with the ya' vocalized (fatḥa) is that of the Shamī (Syrian) reader. The meaning is: when a believer cannot easily perform worship in the land where he is, and the affairs of his religion are not made smooth for him, then let him emigrate from it to a land where he judges that his heart will be more sound, his religion more correct, and his worship more abundant. The lands differ greatly in this respect. They said: "We have not found anything more helpful in subduing the self, more gathering for the heart, more encouraging of contentment, more effective in driving away Satan, further from trials, or more binding to the religious duty than Makkah, may God Most High protect it." It is related from Sahl: "When sins and innovations appear in a land, then leave it for a land of the obedient." It is related from the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a span of land, has earned Paradise."

﴿So worship Me﴾. The ya' is read in the reading of Yaʿqūb. Its underlying form is: fa-iyyāya fa-ʿbudūnī (so it is Me alone that you should worship, and worship Me). The fā' is used in fa-ʿbudūn because it is the answer (jawāb) of an elided conditional clause (sharṭ maḥdhūf), since the meaning is: "Indeed My earth is vast; so if you do not devote your worship sincerely to Me in one land, then devote it in another." Then the conditional was elided, and in its place the object was fronted (taqdīm al-mafʿūl), which conveys the meaning of exclusivity (ikhtiṣāṣ) and sincerity (ikhlāṣ). Then he encouraged the emigrant with his saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 57:

﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾ That is: it will find its bitterness and its anguish just as the one who tastes perceives the flavour of what is tasted, for when it is certain of death, leaving its homeland becomes easy for it. ﴿Then to Us you will be returned﴾ after death, for reward and punishment. (The reading) yurja'un (they will be returned) is from Yahya; (the reading) tarji'un (you will be returned) is from Ya'qub.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 58:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely settle them in the Garden in lofty chambers﴾ (We will surely make them descend from the Garden into lofty chambers). (p-684) "لَنُثْوِيَنَّهُمْ" (we will surely lodge them) is read by al-Kufi (the reading of the Kufans) except ʿĀṣim, from al-thawā' (dwelling, lit. "staying"), which means descending for the purpose of residence. Thawā is intransitive; when made transitive by adding the hamza (ith'āl, causative form), it does not govern more than one object. The justification for its governing the pronoun of the believers and the chambers (al-ghuraf) is either that it is treated as if it were lananzilannahum (we will surely make them descend), or as if it were lanu'wiyannahum (we will surely shelter them), or that the preposition is omitted and the verb made to reach its object directly, or that the temporal adverbial (al-ẓarf al-muwaqqat, a time-limited adverb) is treated as an indefinite (al-mubham, unspecified) one. ﴿Beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. How excellent is the reward of those who act﴾. It may be pausing (waqf) on "al-ʿāmilīn" (those who act) on the basis that "anna" (that)

Those who are patient: this is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning "they are those who have been patient" over leaving their homelands, over the harm of the polytheists, over trials and calamities, over acts of obedience, and over refraining from sins. Connecting it (to the preceding words) is better, so that "those who" serves as an attributive qualifier (na't) of "those who act." ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾. They did not rely upon anyone in all of that except Allah.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered those who had embraced Islam in Makkah to emigrate (hijrah), they feared poverty and loss of livelihood. So this was revealed: ﴿And how many a creature (dabbah) does not carry its provision﴾. That is: "And how many a creature..." The word "ka'ayyin" (how many) with the long vowel and hamza is the reading of Ibn Kathir (Makkan). The dabbah is every living being that crawls upon the face of the earth, whether it has reason or not. ﴿It does not carry its provision﴾: it is not able to carry it, due to its weakness in bearing it. ﴿Allah provides for it and for you﴾: that is, none provides for those weak creatures except Allah, and none provides for you, O strong ones, except Him either, even though you are able to carry your provisions and earn them. For if He had not provided for you and had not provided for you the means of earning, you would be more incapable than the creatures that cannot carry. It is reported from al-Hasan: "It does not carry its provision" means it does not store it; rather it wakes in the morning and Allah provides for it. It was also said: no animal stores food except the son of Adam, the mouse, and the ant. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of your saying, "We fear poverty and destitution," ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what is in your inner thoughts.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 61:

﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?"﴾ That is: and if you asked these polytheists, "Who created the heavens and the earth, despite their vastness and expanse, and who is it that subjected the sun and the moon?" ﴿They would surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾ (p-685) That is, how are they turned away from the Oneness of Allah, given their acknowledgment of all of this?

Allah extends provision to whomever He wills of His servants, and restricts it for him. (Qur'an 29:62, first part)

That is, "for whomever He wills," so the pronoun (الضمير, al-ḍamīr) was placed in the position of مَن يَشاءُ (man yashā'). This is because مَن يَشاءُ is indefinite and unspecified, so the pronoun was likewise indefinite, like it. قَدَرَ الرِزْقَ وقَتَرَهُ means, in effect, that he restricted the provision and narrowed it, when he constricted it.

﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of everything.﴾ He knows what benefits His servants and what corrupts them.

In a hadith: "Among My servants there are those whose faith is not made right except by wealth, and if I made them poor it would corrupt them. And among My servants there are those whose faith is not made right except by poverty, and if I made them wealthy it would corrupt them."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 63:

﴿And if you were to ask them, "Who sends down water from the sky and with it revives the earth after its death?" they would surely say, "Allah."﴾ That is: they acknowledge this.

﴿Say: "All praise is for Allah."﴾ For His sending down water to revive the earth; or because He is among those who acknowledge something similar to what they acknowledged, and then that acknowledgment benefited him in affirming the oneness of Allah and negating partners from Him, and it was not an idle acknowledgment like the acknowledgment of the polytheists.

﴿But most of them do not understand.﴾ They do not reflect, though they have within them intellects, upon the signs We show them and the proofs We establish for them. Or: they do not understand what you mean by your saying "All praise is for Allah."

﴿And this worldly life is only amusement and play.﴾ That is: it is only like children playing for a while and then dispersing, because of how quickly it passes away from its people and because of their death from it. In this there is a belittling of the world and a diminishing of its affair. And how could it not be diminished, when it does not weigh a gnat's wing in His sight? Lahw (amusement) is whatever a person takes pleasure in, which distracts him for a time and then comes to an end. ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode—that is the [true] life.﴾ Al-Hayawan means al-hayah (life). That is, there is in it only a lasting, enduring life, with no death in it, so it is in its very essence life. Al-Hayawan is the masdar (verbal noun) of hayya, and its analogical form is hayayan, so the second yā' was changed into wāw (hayawan). He did not say al-hayah (life) because the pattern fa'alan carries the meaning of movement and agitation, and life is movement while death is stillness. Its coming in a pattern that indicates movement is an intensification of the meaning of life. It is to be pause-stopped on al-hayawan, because the sense is: ﴿if only they knew﴾ the reality of the two abodes, they would not have chosen the perishing amusement over the enduring life. Had it been connected [to what follows], the description of the Hayawan would have become conditional upon their knowing that, and that is not the case.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 65:

﴿When they board the ship﴾ is connected to an omitted element indicated by what He described them with and explained of their state; its meaning: they are in the condition they were described with, of polytheism and obstinacy, so when they board the ship, ﴿they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion﴾, existing in the form of those among the believers who devote religion purely to God, in that they mention none but God and call upon no other god along with Him. ﴿But when He brings them safely to land﴾ and they feel secure, ﴿behold, they associate partners [with Him]﴾, returning to the state of polytheism.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 66:

﴿لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ﴾ [They are ungrateful for what We have given them] of the blessing. It has been said that the lam here is the lam of purpose (lam kay), and likewise in ﴿وَلِيَتَمَتَّعُوا﴾ [and that they may enjoy themselves] for the one who reads it with a kasra, meaning: "so that they may disbelieve, and so that they may enjoy themselves." The meaning is: they return to their polytheism so that by returning to their polytheism they become disbelievers in the blessing of deliverance, intending only to enjoy it and take pleasure in it and nothing else. This is contrary to the custom of the sincere believers in truth, who give thanks for God's blessing when He delivers them, and who make the blessing of deliverance a means to increased obedience, not to pleasure and enjoyment. On this reading, there is no pause at ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ [they associate partners]. As for the one who takes it as the lam of command (lam al-amr), with the reading of Ibn Kathir, Hamza and Ali, "وَلْيَتَمَتَّعُوا" with a sukun on the lam, it is in the sense of a threat, like His saying ﴿فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾ [Al-Kahf: 29] ["So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve"]. Its verification is in usul al-fiqh (the principles of jurisprudence), which you may consult. ﴿فَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [But they will come to know] the evil of their scheming when they are destroyed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 67:

﴿Have they not seen﴾ That is: the people of Makkah, ""that We have made"" their town ﴿a sanctuary (haram)﴾, protected and secure, ﴿safe (aminan)﴾, whoever enters it being safe, ﴿while people are being snatched away from around them﴾, that is, they are plundered, killed and taken captive.

(p-687) ﴿Will they then believe in falsehood﴾, that is, in the Satan and the idols, ﴿and be ungrateful for the blessing of Allah﴾, that is, for Muhammad (ﷺ) and Islam? ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him? Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 68]

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 29, verse 68:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah,﴾ by ascribing to Him a partner, ﴿or denies the truth﴾ — the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Book — ﴿when it has come to him.﴾ That is: they did not hesitate in denying it when they heard it. ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers?﴾ This is an affirmation of their dwelling in Hell, because when the interrogative hamza of denial (hamzat al-inkar) enters upon a negation, it becomes an affirmation. The meaning is: Will they not dwell therein, when they have fabricated this kind of lie against Allah and denied the truth with this kind of denial? Or: Is it not established for them that there is an abode in Hell for the disbelievers, when they have dared such daring? The mention of "abode" (mathwa) in opposition to ﴿We will surely settle them﴾ supports the reading of the second (form).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 29, verse 69:

﴿Those who strive﴾: He used "striving" (*mujahadah*) without specifying an object, so that it covers everything that must be striven against: the self (*nafs*), Satan, and the enemies of the religion. ﴿for Us﴾: for Our sake, on Our account, and seeking Our face sincerely. ﴿We shall surely guide them to Our paths﴾. Abu 'Amr read "*subulana*" (in the singular form, "Our path"). That is, "We shall surely increase them in guidance to the paths of good and in success (*tawfiq*)." It is also reported from al-Darani: "Those who strive, in what they know, We shall guide them to what they do not know." It has been said: whoever acts on what he knows is granted success in what he does not know. It has also been said: the ignorance you see in us regarding what we do not know is only due to our failure in what we do know. It is reported from Fudayl: "Those who strive in seeking knowledge, We shall guide them to the paths of acting upon it." It is reported from Sahl: "Those who strive in establishing the *sunnah* (the prophetic way), We shall guide them to the paths of Paradise." It is reported from Ibn 'Ata': "They strove in seeking Our pleasure; We shall guide them to reaching the place of good pleasure (*ridwan*)." It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "They strove in obeying Us; We shall guide them to the paths of Our reward." It is reported from al-Junayd: "They strove in repentance; We shall guide them to the paths of sincerity." Or: "They strove in serving Us; We shall open for them the paths of intimate conversation with Us (*munajah*) and companionship with Us (*uns*)." Or: "They strove in seeking Us, aiming for Our pleasure; We shall guide them to the paths of reaching Us." ﴿And indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾: with victory and assistance in this world, and with reward and forgiveness in the Hereafter.
